title: Primitive sums of powerful integers and the abc endpoint
summary: A strict primitive-triple exponent derived from explicitly stated small-budget abc box hypotheses, a reverse transfer by the least target multiplier, and an independent determinant saving of 1/(153k).
abstract:
Assuming two stated small-budget \(abc\) box estimates, we obtain
\(O_{p,q,r,\eps}(X^{(1/3-\delta)\lambda_0+\eps})\) for the count of ordered primitive
\(p,q,r\)-full triples \(a+b=c\le X\), where
\(\lambda_0=1/p+1/q+1/r\) is sufficiently small and
\(\delta>0\) is absolute. Fullness forces point masses at the
limiting one-third coefficient.
A congruence determinant gives
\(O_{k,\eps}(X^{(2-1/153)/k+\eps})\) for large equal orders \(k\)
and an order-\(1/r\) saving for large \(r\) at fixed offsets.
Pointwise counts of two \(k\)-full summands are
\(O_\eps(N^{3/10+\eps})\) for \(k=2\) and \(O_{k,\eps}(N^{1/(k+1)+\eps})\)
for \(k\ge3\). Under the box hypotheses, a saving in a count with least
target multipliers is equivalent to a strict saving for small-budget \(abc\) triples.

verification.scope: Proof review of the strict transfer and the two directions of the repair equivalence under the named endpoint hypotheses. Prior written graph and determinant proofs are retained. The current edition includes fresh exact parameter and certificate replays, a standalone LaTeX build, and layout review. An internal PDF-only reader review informed the final wording and verification links.
verification.limits: The full analytic proof of the endpoint hypotheses remains outside this manuscript and needs specialist review. External specialist review, formal verification and a broader literature comparison remain unperformed.

next_steps: Review the full proof chain for the limiting one-third box bound and endpoint balance and nonatomic mass, including the signed monomial counts, real strips and congruence amplification.
Obtain specialist review of the explicit determinant count, the radical-sector equivalence and their verification files.
Seek a uniform saving for distinct least-multiplier quotients in the balanced radical sector of Theorem 20.
